steps.title: Boolean operations
steps.body: work on Boolean values (TRUE and FALSE) to produce a Boolean result. They are used to combine or invert conditions in IF statements and WHILE loops.

steps.title: NOT
steps.body: reverses a Boolean value. NOT TRUE = FALSE, NOT FALSE = TRUE. It is used to invert a condition.

steps.title: AND
steps.body: returns TRUE only when BOTH conditions are TRUE. If either one is FALSE, the result is FALSE.

steps.title: OR
steps.body: returns TRUE when at least ONE condition is TRUE. Only returns FALSE when BOTH conditions are FALSE.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Complete the truth table for A AND B where A = TRUE, B = FALSE. | Evaluate: NOT (TRUE OR FALSE) | Use De Morgan's Laws to simplify: NOT (x >= 0 AND x <= 100)

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: TRUE AND FALSE = FALSE. Both must be TRUE for AND to return TRUE. | TRUE OR FALSE = TRUE. Then NOT TRUE = FALSE. | Using De Morgan's: NOT(x >= 0) OR NOT(x <= 100) = x < 0 OR x > 100.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Memorise the truth tables for NOT, AND, and OR AND needs BOTH to be TRUE; OR needs at least ONE Use brackets whenever combining AND and OR in the same condition De Morgan's: NOT(AND) becomes OR of NOTs, NOT(OR) becomes AND of NOTs Precedence: NOT first, then AND, then OR When simplifying conditions, apply De Morgan's Laws to make code clearer
